I just wanna say. This contest was an absolute blast, and produced an absolute truckload of great content. I'm glad to have participated!

I would implore everyone to take some time and get around to reading all of these entries, at your own pace. Due to the massive density of content, a lot of works ended up sorely underrated and underexposed, and that's a shame, because there are some absolute gems in here.

item.title: CONTEST UPDATE
item.content:encoded:
Hey all!

So, we got some 130-something entries, which is just fucking fantastic. I'm legitimately stunned, I wasn't expecting a third of that number. This is the first contest ARD and I have run as captains of Community Outreach, and the results have been inspiring.

And the average quality of the work is superb as well, meaning most of this stuff will stay around, which is also capital-G Great.

However, this leads to a problem. People have lives, and jobs, and things to do, and expecting people to be able to read 130 entries in the space of a week is fairly unreasonable. It's a good problem to have, but that doesn't mean it's not a problem.

As such, we will be extending the voting period for one week (with a possible extension later) to make it easier for people to read all the entries. The timers will be changed sometime this evening. So go out there and vote!

item.title: In mercy's name, three days are all I need...
item.content:encoded:
While the results were certainly nowhere near my best work, the pressure to conceive of, write, and post an article in 24 hours was pretty exhilarating, especially for someone like me who takes half a year to hammer out an article. I posted all three days, and I'm pretty happy with my contributions overall:

Murder Mystery: SCP-3937, "Site-112"
Tropical: "Minutes of the 383rd General Meeting of the Coharmonius Pelagic Society, Concerning an Unexpected Pugilistic Threat"
Dark & Stormy Night: SCP-3164, "Character Test"

Who knows if any of these will stay on the wiki, but they were certainly fun to write. I'm looking forward to JamCon II next year because that's a thing, right?

item.title: All Three Days!
item.content:encoded:
Wow, this contest was a blast, if also tiring as all hell. I wrote for all three days, with moderate success! I am proud of most of my work here which I am happy about.

My murder mystery! I'm not going to lie, I am disappointed with how few people caught my few hidden clues that not all in the original case was how it seemed, but it was incredibly fun to write nonetheless.] (also, if you figure it out, pm me and receive a crisp virtual high five!)

My time crunch one. I got super crunched on Sunday and ended up making a half-baked creepypasta as a joke that I had made about a Donkey Kong game having the word tropical in it. I am glad I wrote it and I got some nice Do's and Don't's of body horror.

My first -J class skip! This was arguably the most fun I have had writing a skip yet. I am also surprised how few people picked up on the way it was a nursery rhyme joke with some odd Foundation elements and literalism thrown in. (Also, I attached it to my first skip because I could not think of a good number for it :P.

Anyway, thank you for any potential reads! Please give me any criticisms you have, as I am always trying to improve my writing style and prose.

Much love to all of the other participants!

-Stallmantic

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Now that the submission period is over, let's have a postmortem of the contest.

Pros: Encourages creative expression and exploration of the various themes.

Cons: Excessive entries might be information overload for voters. And significant entries are not voted as highly as what one might expect from a contest. At least in most other contests, we can see the potential winners with relative ease. Here, it's a bit more complicated.

Recommendations: I think we can rework this into periodic site-wide challenges based on a single theme (and nothing else) under a time-based constraint (post by this date in this timezone). In fact, we can have contests (with judges, rules and detailed management/elaboration) and challenges (free and easy; try if you like; interpret the given theme however you like) as two categories of things for users to exercise their writing acumen.

As I said before, I really like what this contest made me do creatively. I just recently started writing SCPs again and this was a really fun way to think outside the box and get back to why I joined this wiki in the first place: scary and/or weird shit. While these aren't my best work, I'm surprised at how well they turned out and would love to do something like this again. I reiterate my suggestion to use this "theme" idea on a recurring basis.

But who cares about my writing process? Here are the final products!

SCP-3795 - WHO KILLED YOUR DOG?! (Murder Mystery)

This has been the most fun I've had writing since the friggin' Halloween contest. Speaking of, this is the most I've coldposted since then.

Murder Mystery: SCP-3167 Character Assassin (Or: the Serial Killer). Dumb idea I had based off of a dumb pun, and it's probably the dumbest skip I've ever made— it's the first coldposted skip that's survived.

Tropical: Dr. Keith Partridge and the Strawberry Banana Smoothie of DOOM!. The fun of this came from the title. IT was originally going to be "The Smoothie Bar of DOOM!" but I liked the idea of Site-87 being turned into a jungle temporarily. Expect this locale to appear in future S & C Plastics tales.

It was a dark and stormy night: Hotline: Eventide. My tribute to the bizarre Hotline Miami games, set in a new anomalous Nexus that's essentially the exact opposite of Sloth's Pit. A bank robbery during a perpetually dark and stormy night.

ARD, Coony, ILU both. Marry me? :3c
